implementation_notes: Rust reduces duplication in one place and increases it in another. It reduces it because macros and generics express shapes that other languages duplicate, and because a `match` on an enum has no missing arms. It increases it because `#[derive]` and the `From`/`TryFrom` boilerplate have no blanket implementation for most shapes, so the same twenty-line conversion is written for every type — which is exactly the kind of mechanical, parametric duplication that merges cleanly into a macro. `cargo clippy`'s `duplicate_mod` and `same_item_push` plus `cargo udeps` for the unused half are the relevant instruments.
idiom_name: copy-pasted match arms; duplicated From impls
pitfalls: A macro introduced to remove duplication hides the code from every tool that reads syntax, including clone detectors and some IDE navigation.
Merging two `From` impls whose field maps differ produces a macro with field-name arguments, which is harder to read than the two impls.
`clippy::too_many_lines` on a macro-generated expansion is a false positive that makes the linter hard to trust.
